correctness.rationale: Exact Cramer determinant identity for arbitrary lines; uniform bound forcing 1/t angle collision tubes; double collisions and endpoint seam have O(t^-2) probability; single-collision scaling and dominated convergence give coefficient 6v times squared angular density, and insertions of bounded test functions give the marked law. Tail-integral moments and Cauchy–Schwarz optimization complete the deductions. Independent Cartesian recomputation, scaled-pair perturbations, and seeded Monte Carlo passed. Finite computations are corroboration, not proof.

originality.rationale: The exact tangent-circle and curvature-width published theorems establish related 1/t tails under tied support heights and bounded supporting-halfplane constraints, but neither implies the variance-only arbitrary independent signed-offset theorem or its joint size-biased marked limit. Finch 2011 derives one-side marginals; Beermann et al. study small Poisson cells; Daley et al. fix one side and study a different direction model. Full-text priority for Daley et al. remains unresolved.
residual_risks: The full text of Daley–Ebert–Swift (2014) was not accessible; its area formula could conceal partially overlapping tail observations, though its normalized-side model differs.
Earlier stochastic-geometry literature may contain the same variance-universal marked limit under different line coordinates.
Search/database absence is not a historical uniqueness proof.

value.rationale: A natural random-three-line triangle has a universal 1/t large-area mechanism determined by offset variance alone and an exact angular L2 cost. The marked result identifies offset size-bias, angular localization, and a universal uniform collision mark, meaningful beyond a scalar tail. The optimizer yields a sharp design principle and holds for non-Gaussian and atomic offset noise.
